Prof. Fessenbecker was simply fantastic all around. A very enthusiastic and encouraging teacher, he never once turned us down when we approached him with inane questions, and I have to admit there were a considerable amount of them. What also assured me of his endless fount of patience was that everyone knew that everyone else at best skimmed over the readings most of the time, and even though the format of the course was clearly meant for THOROUGH reading of the text supported by heated class discussion, Prof. Fessenbecker never once got mad at us for coming to class so woefully underprepared. I feel a great sense of guilt, for having squandered my last chance at becoming a grand philosopher, and mostly because I constantly underperformed in this class—but there is nothing negative I can say about the teacher himself. Hope he gets more studious students in the future! His classes were a blast.

He could care so much less if we wanted to, and it would be fine, but he is always on top of his game. Very smart and energetic, and I think he structured the syllabus in a genius way. Generally a great person and great instructor.

The texts we were expected to read were very difficult, but Prof. Fessenbecker always made sure to thoroughly explain any difficult concepts, and gently nudge us in the direction of criticially analysing the material at hand. The strongest aspect of the course probably WOULD have been, and still pretty much was, class discussion; but as I said the entire class came unprepared most of the time and it sort of challenged that—but not entirely! Prof. Fessenbecker still managed to get us engaged in discussion and argue endlessly about the readings with what meager preparationg we arrived with. Overall I can’t come up with a particular weakness.
